data.title: The Light That Stayed On
data.excerpt: The porch light in that house stayed on until morning. Not because someone forgot to turn it off, but because someone was still hoping.
content: The porch light had been on every night for twenty years.
When people asked, Mrs. Ellis always said she simply forgot to turn it off.
Her son had left home when he was nineteen after an argument that lasted less than ten minutes.
He promised he would come back when he was ready.
Mrs. Ellis grew older, but the light remained.
One winter morning, a small package appeared on the porch.
Inside was a photograph of a young family standing in front of a house.
On the back were six words:
"Mom, I think I'm ready to come home."
That evening, for the first time in twenty years, Mrs. Ellis turned the porch light off.
